source.title: The Geometry of Refusal: Why Post-Hoc Safety Is Fragile and Pretraining-Time Safety Persists
source.authors: Srikanth Malla; Chi-Ho Choi; J. Choi

page_placements.theme: Behaviour analogue: refusal/safety training and harmful-behaviour unlearning undone by fine-tuning, ablation, priming and jailbreaks

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper presents new results refining the fragility claim: it distinguishes post-hoc suppression from erasure and tests benign fine-tuning attacks, while also testing a pretraining-time counter-method.
record.gate_note: The paper tests refusal behavior and general capability probes, not targeted-knowledge accuracy after unlearning. Its benign-SFT results measure changes in refusal or harmful-output classification, not restoration of forgotten facts. It does not test quantization, prompt-only recovery, or activation-direction ablation itself. Cites of other unlearning and ablation studies are not recorded as results. Values used only to select settings are omitted.
record.test_reason: The study measures refusal of harmful prompts after post-hoc safety training (DPO/RLHF/instruct tuning) and after from-scratch safety co-training. It does not apply any unlearning method or measure targeted-knowledge accuracy. Its suppression-vs-erasure geometry concerns refusal installs on general capability probes, not forgotten facts. The authors cite unlearning (WMDP/RMU, Lynch et al.) only as a contrast, saying it targets the erasure regime. Refusal is a related but different construct, so the findings go under fits_no_version, and no version (A–F) is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that post-hoc safety updates land in a suppression regime that masks rather than removes capability, so benign fine-tuning erodes refusal by 35–38 pp. Continuous co-training loses only 2–14 pp (regex), and persistence rather than timing drives robustness. They add that they do not measure capability after the attack. They also say unlearning targets a different (erasure) regime that they do not study.
record.recipe_differences: The study does not apply the cited unlearning methods. It measures post-hoc DPO/instruct weight changes and benign-SFT vulnerability, then tests safety co-training from scratch. It does not test quantization, activation ablation, or prompt-only recovery.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome varies with benchmark distribution and refusal detector. Co-training refusal is stronger on the AdvBench-like training distribution than on HarmBench or StrongReject; the classifier often reports more erosion than regex. Schedule also matters: safety training that persists to the end installs refusal, while the equal-total-weight windowed schedule does not.

fits_no_version.finding: 100 benign Alpaca examples cut AdvBench refusal of Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct (93.0→58.2) and Llama-3-8B-Instruct (49.2→10.9). Qwen ends below its own base's 71.1% refusal. The classifier shows smaller drops for Qwen.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign fine-tuning erodes post-hoc refusal training in open instruct models.

fits_no_version.finding: Post-hoc safety/instruct weight updates lie 2–3 orders of magnitude below an erasure threshold in Fisher-subspace overlap, which the authors read as suppression rather than erasure.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-hoc refusal training gates rather than erases underlying capability, as shown in weight-space geometry.

fits_no_version.finding: From-scratch continuous safety co-training keeps 84–91% AdvBench regex refusal after benign-SFT from 410M to 6.9B. Erosion is larger under the classifier. Out-of-distribution refusal is low. A windowed schedule installs none.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety co-training persisting through pretraining yields refusal more robust to benign fine-tuning than post-hoc installs.

record.code_released: not stated; the text says code is included in supplementary material and refers to an anonymized repository, but gives no URL.
record.problems: The study does not test unlearning of targeted knowledge or compare attack recovery with a never-trained-on-knowledge model. Its main attack evaluation uses refusal detectors rather than targeted-knowledge accuracy. The authors note that regex measures refusal-gate wording rather than harmfulness; classifier scores differ. Co-training results use one training run per condition, have limited out-of-distribution refusal, and lack a matched-strength post-hoc comparison at 410M. The geometric instrument uses a top-k Fisher approximation; the authors note that tail eigendirections are not measured.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row limit is reached. Left out: additional detailed geometry values (including qnorm and per-layer/per-probe breakdowns in Tables 4–9), safety-only gradient-cosine controls (Tables 14–15), and further co-training schedule, pilot, and stronger-attack conditions (Tables 23–24 and 27 classifier details beyond those retained). These are not additional direct tests of targeted-knowledge recovery; the selected rows retain the main suppression measurements, principal attack outcomes, schedule comparison, and cross-detector results.

untested.parts: No unlearning method and no targeted-knowledge accuracy measured.
Benign Alpaca fine-tuning is applied, but only refusal is measured; no recovery of forgotten knowledge.
No activation-direction ablation. The suppression geometry concerns refusal installs, not unlearning methods or forgotten knowledge.
No unlearning counter-method. Co-training is a refusal-install method tested only against fine-tuning attacks.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's links of geometry rows to C and co-training rows to F conflate refusal/safety alignment with knowledge unlearning. The study's 'capability' means general probes (MMLU, GSM8K, TriviaQA, FLAN), not forgotten target knowledge. The adversarial-SFT erasure control (App. G) is a boundary check, not an unlearning test. The 3-shot and data-loader caveats affect only the co-training rows.

versions.untested_parts: No targeted-knowledge unlearning accuracy near chance is measured, and the paper does not test whether attacks recover targeted knowledge relative to a model that never learned it.
The paper fine-tunes on benign Alpaca examples but measures refusal and harmful-output classifications, not recovery of targeted knowledge or forgotten facts.

The paper analyzes post-hoc safety updates as suppression rather than erasure using general capability probes; it does not ablate an activation direction or directly test recovery of specific unlearned knowledge.
No rephrasing, jailbreak-only, multilingual, or in-context-information recovery experiment.
The paper tests continuous safety co-training against benign fine-tuning and, at one scale, an identity-shifting attack. It does not test quantization, activation ablation, or prompting-only attacks.

relation.reason: Unlearning appears as a contrast in Sec. 2, Sec. 3, App. C and an App. N paragraph. Nothing about unlearning is tested.

tranche.reason: The study applies no unlearning method and measures no targeted-knowledge accuracy. It cites unlearning (WMDP/RMU, Lynch et al.) only as the erasure-regime contrast. T6 fits.

source_check.notes: All rows measure refusal loss after benign SFT, not recovery of unlearned knowledge. Table 1 and the statement's numbers are regex-scored. Under Llama-Guard, Qwen goes 93.0 to 85.2 (Table 25), above its base's 69.5% (Table 10), so 'below its base' holds by regex only. Table 18 states no n or benchmark; its values fit 64 AdvBench prompts. The authors do not measure capability after the attack.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Measured shipped or study-trained post-hoc DPO/instruct updates on the reported capability probes
reader_labels.reason: The measured updates have small Fisher-subspace overlap relative to the stated erasure boundary, which the authors interpret as suppression rather than erasure (R54–R57).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Continuous co-training on AdvBench, regex-scored, across 410M to 6.9B
reader_labels.reason: After benign-SFT, refusal remains 84.0% to 90.6% on the scale runs (R19, R22, R25, R28).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Continuous co-training on out-of-distribution HarmBench and StrongReject, and classifier scoring
reader_labels.reason: Refusal is much lower or falls substantially on out-of-distribution sets, and classifier scoring shows greater erosion than regex scoring on AdvBench (R20–R21, R23–R24, R26–R27, R29–R30, R31–R42).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Windowed schedule versus schedules that persist to the end
reader_labels.reason: The equal-total-weight windowed schedule installs little refusal, while the continuous and post-substrate schedules retain high refusal after attack (R43–R53).
